evidence: Cic. Sen. 72: ut nāvem, ut aedificium

terms.gloss: a massive structure (a pier, a dam, a great pile)
evidence: Hor. C. 3.29.10: mōlem propinquam nūbibus; Caes. BC 1.25 (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: masonry, a way of building; a structure

evidence: Lewis & Short: “a putting or placing together … (in good prose; most freq. in Cic.)”

phrases.latin: ut nāvem, ut aedificium īdem dēstruit facillimē quī cōnstrūxit
phrases.english: just as the man who built a ship or a building takes it apart most easily

phrases.latin: vēneram in suburbānum meum et querēbar dē impēnsīs aedificiī dīlābentis
phrases.english: I had come out to my place near town and was complaining about what the crumbling building was costing me
